reasons: intent_insensitive: question four is no: a different enemy intent would not have changed the line, so the intent is not part of the decision

answers.q1_what_did_you_play: I played Powder Pop first to deal 5 damage and gain 1 Spark, then played Ka-pow! spending that Spark for 7 damage, then played Duck and Cover for 5 Block, and finally played Kaboom! for 7 damage. This used 2 energy and left 1 unused.
answers.q2_other_line_considered: I briefly considered Powder Pop, Ka-pow!, and Kaboom! without Duck and Cover, since the enemy only attacks for 4 and I could survive it. I rejected it because the block was available with remaining energy and had no downside on this turn.
answers.q3_what_it_gave_up: It gave up the option of taking the 4 damage and leaving one energy unused, and it gave up Tinder Toss's 4 all-enemy damage in favor of Ka-pow!'s 7 single-target damage. With one enemy and no other playable cards, those alternatives were inferior.
answers.q4_different_intent: No. A different intent would not have changed the line: Powder Pop still enables Ka-pow!, and Duck and Cover still uses energy that would otherwise be unused. If the enemy attacked harder, block would be more valuable; if it did not attack, block would still not hurt.
